### 🦸 Characters that play differently
- Every character now has its own attributes — health, move speed, jump, magazine size and reload speed — so who you pick actually changes how you play. The Sniper reloads fastest but is fragile and slow; the Heavy soaks damage and carries big mags but lumbers; the Scout is the fastest flanker with a quick reload but thin-skinned. Damage stays equal for everyone — no character can out-gun another just by being picked.
- Every character also has a signature **Q ability**:
  - **Soldier — Adrenaline:** instant reload and +25% damage for a few seconds.
  - **Sniper — X-ray:** see enemies outlined through walls for a few seconds.
  - **Heavy — Bunker:** take 60% less damage, but you can only crawl.
  - **Scout — Agility:** passive double jump and the fastest feet on the roster.
  - **Commander — Reinforcement:** call in a temporary AI soldier to fight at your side.
  - **Commando — Cloak:** turn nearly invisible for a few seconds — no shadow, no floating gun or nametag to give you away.
  - **Terrorist — Suicide charge:** arm a charge that ticks faster and faster, then detonates a huge blast that kills everyone nearby — and you. Everyone around hears the countdown.
  - **Fanatic — Bloodbath:** for 8 seconds your hits heal you — past full health, into an overshield of up to +50 that drains away after the window ends.
  - **Mercenary — Airstrike:** press Q to open the map (you keep walking while you aim), click a point, and a salvo of rockets comes down on it. The target zone is marked with a red ring on the ground and on everyone's map, and each rocket whistles on the way in, so anyone who moves in time gets clear. While you're picking, the map shows every enemy.
- You hear other players' abilities go off near you.
- The Profile shows each character's attributes and ability (effect length, cooldown, once per life or always on), and the HUD shows your ability with its cooldown and active countdown.

### 🎮 Smoother first steps
- New players jump straight in — you get a generated name on first launch and can change it in the Profile any time. No more "set a name first" wall.
- The Profile saves as you type (with a Saving… / Saved badge). Signing in is optional — only needed to keep your character, name and maps across devices.
- Character portraits in the lobby are lit like the game itself, at a slight three-quarter turn, instead of flat and grey.

### 💣 Throwing and guns
- Grenades have two distinct throws: an underhand swing on left click and a short toss to your feet on right click.
- A thrown grenade now leaves your actual hand instead of popping into the middle of the screen at full size.
- A gun you drop keeps the ammo left in its magazine — dropping and picking it back up is no longer a free reload.
- Spawn weapons start with your character's magazine size straight away.

### 🎥 Camera and map
- Third-person view is now the host's choice for the whole room, so everyone in a match shares the same camera.
- The minimap in arena maps now shows the map's real ground colours and water instead of a flat floor.

### 🎬 The sixth test
- Starting a new survival world now opens with a scene: four days after the bite, strapped to a gurney, still talking — and a sister with a plan for the gate.
- It plays once per world. A new game plays it again; continuing one you already started does not.
- Skippable at any point with the on-screen button.

### 🏥 Medical & lab props
- Five new props for the map and structure editors, under a new Medical & Lab category: a hospital gurney, a drip stand, a vitals monitor, a supply trolley and a wall cabinet.
- Shots pass between the gurney's side rails instead of stopping on thin air.

### 👀 Faces that are alive
- Characters in a scene blink, and their jaws move while they speak.
